assignment_description:
Los Soldados, A Terrible Mistake
⍞ Materials: In the Shadow of the Alamo

➜ INTRO
This is an historical fiction book that takes place in 1835-1836. This genre of book allows you to walk in the shoes of the soldiers of Mexico who were forced to fight the Americans at the Battle of Alamo. As you read you will see Spanish terms in italics. You can find the meaning of those words at the back of the book.

➜ LOCATE
∞ Map Link: Mexico
Find Guanajuato which is located in central Mexico, about 130 miles northwest of Mexico City. How would you describe the terrain of this area?
Lorenzo lives in this village.

➜ READ, NARRATE, & DISCUSS
Ch.1-part of ch.2, p.1-14 Beginning-"frown on her face."

• How would you describe Lorenzo so far?

➜ VIEW
The predominant religion of Mexico is Roman Catholicism. Our Lady of Guadalupe holds a special place in the religious life of Mexico and is one of the most popular religious devotions. Her image, of a woman of mixed Indigeneous and European features wearing a turquoise-colored mantle surrounded by a sunburst, has played an important role as a national symbol of Mexico.
∞ Image Link: Virgin of Guadalupe

Showdown in Paris
⍞ Materials: Eiffel's Tower for Young People, notebook

➜ INTRO
When you think of Paris, what image comes to mind? For most people, it is the Eiffel Tower. But did you know that many people were against the building of the Eiffel Tower and many obstacles almost prevented the Eiffel Tower from being built. This book will tell that story. It also tells the story about what life was like at the end of the 19th century and introduces us to people from around the world. A list of the people mentioned in this book are listed on p. ix-xi. It might helpful to look back at it as you read.

➜ READ, NARRATE, & DISCUSS
1.Begin Ch.1, p.1-19 (Read the narrative and skip blue pages) Beginning-"terrible for an artist!"
2.(Optional) Blue pages on p.4-5

• Why do you think it was important for the French to build something taller than the Americans?

➜ VIEW
1.This 555-foot stone pillar was the tallest human-made structure at the time.
∞ Image Link: Washington Monument
2\. You can view a few of the paintings of James McNeill Whistler, the American painter based in England, known for post-impressionism.
∞ Link: Paintings of James McNeill Whistler

➜ NOTEBOOK
Each chapter features recurring characters who were connected in some way to the 1889 World’s Fair. Create a graphic organizer that will help you keep track of the individuals that you will encounter in this text. You will add to this page when you encounter the character again in a subsequent chapter.
